B1.3 Flowcharts and Pseudocode

Make algorithm logic readable and testable

"Handle admissions quickly." That is not an algorithm.

Goals are broad. Algorithms need decisions, branches, and outputs.

What has to become explicit before coding starts?

Natural language to pseudocode

INPUT attendance, feesPaid
IF attendance >= 90 AND feesPaid = TRUE THEN
    OUTPUT "Approved"
ELSE
    OUTPUT "Hold"
END IF

Pseudocode strips language syntax but keeps decision and branch logic precise.

Ambiguity test

Rewrite this so two developers produce identical logic:

"If score is close to pass, allow retake."

Define exact threshold values and branch outcomes.

Then: algorithm precision worksheet in Activities.

Pseudocode is communication, not decoration.

If input, process, decision, and output are unclear, the algorithm is unclear.

Use consistent pseudocode conventions

Need Clear form
Input INPUT value
Process total ← total + value
Decision IF condition THEN ... ELSE ... END IF
Output OUTPUT result

Flowcharts fail at the decision points.

Most errors come from unlabeled branches or broken connectors.

How do we prevent branch ambiguity?

Flowchart quality rules

  • Use standard symbols for process, input/output, and decision.
  • Label every decision branch clearly (Yes/No or True/False).
  • Make each branch reconnect or terminate without dead ends.
  • Trace one test case to validate the algorithm path.

Find the weak branch

Given a flawed flowchart, identify:

  • One missing decision label
  • One broken branch connector
  • One algorithm path that cannot reach output

Then: flowchart correction worksheet in Activities.

Before implementation, how do we prove the logic really works?

Next: tracing algorithms step by step with test data to expose hidden errors.
